one_month_reasoning: Arista's own Q3 2026 report is scheduled for Nov 2, 2026 after the close (source 14), i.e. just OUTSIDE the Oct 30 window, so the main company catalyst does not land inside it. In-window industry read-throughs: hyperscaler Q3 prints (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, late October) with capex commentary for 2027, and Celestica's Q3 (late Oct) which reports 800G/1.6T switch volumes; these are likely supportive (Celestica already guided 2027 growth above 2026's ~65%, Amazon says constraints persist through 2027) but are well known. Stock is near the top of its 52-week range after a strong run, so no momentum tilt beyond a tiny positive drift. I use a near-symmetric lognormal around $204 with monthly vol 54%/3.5 = 15.4%, giving a median just under spot.

fair_value.method: Blend of 12-month-forward P/E (CY2028E EPS ~$6.20 x 32x = ~$200, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (CY2028E FCF ~$7.8B at 2.8% plus ~$13.3B net cash = ~$228, weight 0.4) = ~$211.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: CY2028E non-GAAP EPS $6.20 (CY2027E $5.15 x 1.20) x 32x forward multiple, as the market will price NTM EPS in Sep 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 EPS ~ $4.10 (Q1~0.89 + Q2 1.02 + Q3 1.07 + Q4 ~1.12). 2027 revenue +28% to ~$16.1B: below the DC Ethernet market's +64.5% YoY (IDC 2Q26) because Arista's own growth (+37.6%) lags the market as Nvidia and white-box/Celestica take share, but supported by Celestica guiding 2027 growth above 65% and 1.6T production in 2027. 47% op margin + ~$0.5B interest income, 20% tax, 1.28B diluted shares => ~$5.05; consensus $5.28; blended $5.15.

Broadcom outlines AI semi revenue doubling again 2027->2028, Morgan Stanley sees DC capex $1.3T (2027) -> $1.5T (2028); I haircut to ~20% EPS growth for decelerating base, share pressure from Nvidia Spectrum-X and Cisco (hyperscaler AI revenue guided +88%).

Current forward P/E ~39x on consensus (tickernerd). By Sep 2027 growth decelerates from ~40% to ~20% and share data show Arista 3rd in AI back-end (Dell'Oro) and #2 branded DC vendor behind Nvidia (IDC), so I compress the multiple to ~32x (still premium to Cisco's ~17% EPS growth profile).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: CY2028E FCF ~$7.8B capitalised at 2.8% yield = ~$279B EV, plus ~$13.3B net cash, / 1.28B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: supports FCF running at or above net income
CY2028E net income ~$7.9B (EPS $6.20 x 1.28B) with FCF conversion ~100% given low capex and deferred-revenue build, trimmed slightly for memory inventory build (supply secured through 2027 per call).
Consistent with ~32-35x earnings for a net-cash, 60%+ gross margin franchise; component inflation (Dell'Oro: campus ASP +19% on memory costs) is a margin risk but has been passed through.

bear.story: AI capex digestion signals for 2028 emerge by mid-2027 and/or Arista keeps ceding DC share to Nvidia Spectrum-X, Cisco Silicon One and Celestica white boxes; 2027 growth slows to ~15%, gross margin squeezed by memory costs; multiple de-rates to ~23x on ~$5.8B NTM EPS.

base.story: Industry keeps growing fast (hyperscaler capex toward ~$1T in 2027, 1.6T ramps) but Arista grows ~28% in 2027, below the market, as share drifts; EPS ~$5.15 CY27 / ~$6.20 CY28 at ~32-35x.

bull.story: Supply-constrained industry (Ullal: two-year problem to 2028) favours the vendor with secured supply; scale-across and 1.6T win big at Meta/Microsoft/OpenAI-class customers, 2027 growth 35%+, CY28 EPS ~$7.3 at ~40x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$140 the stock would trade near 22x CY2027E EPS, a level that implies the market sees either a hyperscaler capex cut for 2028 or a structural share loss at a top-2 customer (Meta/Microsoft) to Nvidia or white-box; ordinary volatility (54% realized) rarely takes it there without such news. It is also below the prior 52-week consolidation zone.

key_uncertainties: Share trajectory: DC Ethernet market +64.5% YoY in 2Q26 vs Arista +37.6%; Nvidia now #1 branded DC vendor
Durability of hyperscaler capex into 2028; 2027 capex guides not yet given by Meta/Microsoft
Memory/component inflation vs pricing power on gross margin
Customer concentration (Meta, Microsoft) and white-box (Celestica) displacement
Supply constraints may cap upside but extend the cycle
reasoning: Industry lane evidence: the pie is growing extremely fast (IDC 2Q26 Ethernet switch $18.9B +43%, DC $12.3B +65%; Dell'Oro says AI back-end switch sales passed front-end for the first time; Celestica raised 2026 and says 2027 growth will exceed 2026's 65%; Broadcom sees AI semis $58B->$115B in 2027; Cisco guides hyperscaler AI revenue +88%; hyperscaler capex ~$725B in 2026 heading toward ~$1T). But the chain also shows Arista losing relative share: its DC growth (+37.6%) is well below the market, Nvidia overtook it as #1 branded DC vendor, and it ranks third in AI back-end behind Celestica and Nvidia (partly deferred-revenue timing). Campus is a bright spot (share gains two quarters running, ASP-driven market growth). Company-reported anchors: FY26 guide $12.6B, Q3 guide EPS $1.06-1.08, $13.3B cash, 1.276B shares. Valuation blend gives ~$211, near spot, so I centre the 12-month distribution slightly above spot (mean ~$216) with a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear 135/25%, base 215/50%, bull 295/25%) whose overall dispersion (~45% effective) sits below the 54% realized vol because the stock is a profitable net-cash large cap but above a typical large-cap because it is a levered bet on AI capex. Analyst targets ($225-247 avg) were noted as evidence only. Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so consensus EPS came from web aggregators with conflicting stale figures; I relied on my own build cross-checked with the ~39x forward P/E. X posts were used only as leads.
